findings.finding: M2.2 required PackResolution but depended only on M2.1, so the serializer could be scheduled before the registry lifecycle produced versioned pack resolution.
findings.repair: M2.2 now depends on M2.3-M2.7 and consumes the resulting resolved pack, selection, composition, slot/policy/gap and legacy-migration contracts.

findings.finding: M2.4 consumed query/sector/report/case intent objects without an explicit producer, leaving selection classification ownership ambiguous.
findings.repair: M2.1 now produces NormalizedIntentProfile; M2.4 owns PackSelectionIntentClassifier and consumes validated input plus that profile.

findings.finding: M2.6 needed source-authority policy but no M2 child owned its resolution, risking policy labels without versioned pack provenance.
findings.repair: M2.3 now outputs ResolvedSourceAuthorityPolicySet; M2.6 consumes it alongside PackResolution.

findings.finding: M2.9 required a ModelCompilationProposal even though M2.8 correctly denies model execution by default, making deterministic shadow orchestration semantically dependent on a forbidden path.
findings.repair: M2.9 now consumes ModelAdmissionDecision and DecisionSurfaceBundle; a denied admission is an explicit deterministic-shadow route, not an implicit fallback or model call.

findings.finding: The initial lint checked owner uniqueness and cycles but not whether every consumed contract had a producer reachable through the declared dependency graph.
findings.repair: The lint now validates external-provider declarations, single output ownership and transitive producer-to-consumer dependency closure.
